final_note: Lambda calculus is the theoretical root of functional programming.

concepts.def: Church's formal system of functions and application, 1930s.
A pure, lazy, statically typed functional language.
An influential FP language family from 1958, with code as data.
Delay evaluating an expression until its value is needed.
Evaluate arguments before calling the function.
Lisp's parenthesised notation for code and data.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lambda calculus, developed by Alonzo Church in the 1930s, is Turing-complete using only variables, function abstraction and application. Modern FP languages are essentially typed extensions of it.
Haskell is purely functional and lazy — values are computed only when needed. Its type system catches many bugs at compile time and supports advanced abstractions like monads.
Lisp (1958, John McCarthy) introduced first-class functions, recursion and garbage collection. Code is written as s-expressions — the same lists used for data — enabling powerful macros.
